eaar.title: Enhanced AAR
eaar.subtitle: Enhanced AAR probes with each class's own DSCP. Without it, a SLA class is measured through whichever queue the default probe lands in — so the figures can look healthy while the traffic they claim to describe is being dropped.
eaar.desc.enabled: Every SLA class probes with its own DSCP, and every edge runs a release that supports it.
eaar.desc.partial: Some traffic is still measured with default probes, so part of the SLA data below describes the wrong queue.
eaar.desc.disabled: No app-probe-class is in use. Every SLA figure below is measured with the default probe DSCP.
eaar.all_supported: Every edge runs a release that supports enhanced AAR.
eaar.all_clear: Nothing to fix — enhanced AAR is fully in effect.
eaar.finding.no_probe_classes: No app-probe-class is defined, so every SLA class falls back to default-DSCP probing.
eaar.finding.default_probing: {sla} has no app-probe-class: it is measured with the default probe DSCP, not with the marking of the traffic it governs.
eaar.finding.dangling_probe: {sla} references the app-probe-class {probe}, which does not exist. It looks configured but probes with the default DSCP.
eaar.finding.version_too_old: {host} runs {version} and needs {required} or later before enhanced AAR takes effect on it.
eaar.finding.probe_unused: The app-probe-class {probe} is defined but no SLA class references it.
compat.title: vManage compatibility
compat.subtitle: Which data sources this controller actually served, and how well founded the dashboard's assumptions about each one are.
compat.note.per_device: Cisco's SDK lists this path only with a deviceId parameter; the fabric-wide form used here is unconfirmed.
compat.disclaimer: Only the last column is a fact about the controller in front of you — it records what the last poll received. The evidence column says how each endpoint was arrived at: Catalogued means the exact method and path appear in Cisco's own catalystwan SDK endpoint catalogue; Variant means that catalogue has the path only in another form, normally requiring a deviceId; Unverified means it came from the documented API and has never been validated against a live controller. Treat anything but Catalogued as needing confirmation on your own vManage.
compat.rel.range: Targeted from {minimum}; endpoint audit covers up to {verified_to}.
compat.rel.newer_note: This controller runs {version}, newer than the {verified_to} the audit reaches. Nothing here refuses to run — the source table below records what it actually served.
compat.rel.old_note: This controller runs {version}, older than the {minimum} the dashboard targets. Expect endpoints to be missing or shaped differently.
eaar.assumed_note: {count} edge(s) run {versions}, newer than the release table this check uses. They are taken as capable because the feature predates them, not because that release was verified.
